section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining body image flexibility as a mediator between body size discrepancies and body appreciation in a pre-college sample of White older adolescent females. The study found that compassionate and mindful confrontation of aversive body-related thoughts and emotions partially explained the inverse relationships between body dissatisfaction and body appreciation, with effects retained when controlling for BMI. The authors acknowledge significant limitations including the small, racially-homogenous, non-random sample; cross-sectional design; reliance on self-report measures (including self-reported BMI); and low survey response rate, recommending future prospective and experimental research with more diverse samples.
